what_its_for: Etoposide is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, including small cell lung cancer and testicular cancer. It works by stopping cancer cells from growing and dividing. Your doctor may also use it for other types of cancer not listed here.
how_to_take: Etoposide comes as a capsule to swallow by mouth or as an injection given into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider. If you are taking the capsules at home: Swallow them whole with a full glass of water. You may take them with or without food, but taking them with food may help if you feel nauseous. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules. Always wash your hands before and after handling this medication. If a capsule breaks, avoid touching the contents — it can be harmful to skin.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your body size, type of cancer, and how well your kidneys and liver are working. Doses are highly individual, so never change your dose without talking to your doctor or pharmacist. Etoposide is usually given in cycles — meaning you take it for a few days, then rest for a period of time before the next cycle. Your healthcare team will give you a specific schedule to follow.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, call your doctor or cancer care team right away before taking anything. Do NOT double up or take an extra dose to make up for the one you missed. Because etoposide is part of a carefully planned treatment schedule, your doctor needs to decide the best next step for you.
storage: Store etoposide capsules in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from children and pets at all times. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist or cancer center about the safest way to dispose of leftover medication through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) while on etoposide without asking your doctor first. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase side effects and make nausea worse. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment — etoposide can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time afterward. Talk to your doctor about how long. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you have any of these: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; blood in your urine or stools; extreme tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath or chest pain; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that won't stop; mouth sores that make eating or drinking painful; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; or yellowing of your skin or eyes (which may signal liver problems).
when_it_works: Etoposide starts working right away at the cellular level, but it may take several weeks or cycles of treatment before you or your doctor see measurable results. Your doctor will monitor your progress with blood tests, scans, or other tests throughout your treatment. Everyone responds differently, so be patient and keep all of your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to side effects such as low blood counts and infections. Your doctor may adjust your dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be lowered because your body may not clear the medicine as quickly. Be sure to tell your doctor about any kidney or liver issues. Pregnancy: Do NOT use etoposide if you are pregnant — it can seriously harm or cause birth defects in an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after. Men should use birth control for at least 4 months after treatment ends. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking etoposide, as the drug can pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Children: This medicine can be used in children for certain cancers; the dose will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's body size and condition.
